flawed_step: Lines 165–182 (repeated at 411–429) state the inversion theorem without assuming α(1)≠0; line 439 consequently asserts that the associated system is nonsingular without justification.
counterexample: Set α(n)=0 for every positive integer n and G(X)=1 for X≥1. Then F(X)=∑_{n≤X}α(n)G(X/n)=0 for every X, so the theorem's hypothesis holds. At X=1, however, any claimed expression ∑_{n≤1}β(n)F(1/n) equals 0, while G(1)=1. Moreover, the stated coefficient β(1)=1/α(1)=1/0 is undefined. Thus the theorem is false as stated.
assessment_summary: The inversion formula requires the missing hypothesis α(1)≠0. The proof explicitly relies on it when calling the triangular system nonsingular.
